description: Frequently asked questions about the HAWAQM air quality monitoring system. These are answered directly by the AI without querying the database.

faqs.question: What does a Data Success Rate of 72% mean?
faqs.answer: A Data Success Rate of 72% means HAWAQM received 72% of the data it expected from the deployed devices for the measured period. This is below the minimum target of 75%.

faqs.question: How often do HAWAQM devices record data?
faqs.answer: HAWAQM devices record and transmit measured data at 5-minute intervals.

faqs.question: When is a device considered offline or inactive?
faqs.answer: A device is considered offline or inactive when it has not sent any measured data during the last 24 hours. It becomes active again as soon as it sends new measured data.

faqs.question: When is a site shown as inactive?
faqs.answer: A site is shown as inactive when one or both of its installed devices are inactive. A site used only for mold testing may have no device.

faqs.question: How is the site AQI calculated when a site has more than one device?
faqs.answer: The site AQI is the average of all devices installed at that site. Averaging can soften one high reading, so if a site's figure looks different from what you expect, check the device-level view.

faqs.question: Which air-quality parameters are monitored by HAWAQM?
faqs.answer: HAWAQM monitors CO2, PM10, PM2.5, formaldehyde (CH2O), CO, O3, TVOC, NO2 and benzene, together with ambient noise, temperature and humidity.

faqs.question: Does HAWAQM monitor temperature, humidity and noise as well as pollutants?
faqs.answer: Yes. In addition to gas and particulate measurements, HAWAQM records temperature, humidity and ambient noise.

faqs.question: What AQI range is considered Good?
faqs.answer: An AQI of 0–50 is Good — the cleanest band. The air is fine for everyone and no precautions are needed.

faqs.question: What AQI range is considered Moderate?
faqs.answer: An AQI of 51–100 is Moderate. The air is acceptable for almost everyone; only unusually sensitive people may notice any effect. No action is needed — just keep an eye on it.

faqs.question: What AQI range is Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups?
faqs.answer: An AQI of 101–150 is Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups. People with asthma or heart conditions, young children and older adults may feel effects. At this level it is worth checking the cause.

faqs.question: What AQI range is Unhealthy?
faqs.answer: An AQI of 151–200 is Unhealthy. Everyone may start to feel health effects, and sensitive groups more strongly. The source should be investigated.

faqs.question: What AQI range is Very Unhealthy?
faqs.answer: An AQI of 201–300 is Very Unhealthy. Health effects are likely for everyone in the space. Investigate immediately.

faqs.question: What AQI value is considered Hazardous?
faqs.answer: An AQI above 300 is Hazardous — the most serious level. It is rare indoors, so first verify the reading, then act immediately.

faqs.question: What are the AQI categories or levels?
faqs.answer: There are six AQI categories: An AQI of 0–50 is Good — the air is fine for everyone and no precautions are needed. An AQI of 51–100 is Moderate — acceptable for almost everyone; only unusually sensitive people may notice any effect. An AQI of 101–150 is Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups — people with asthma or heart conditions, young children and older adults may feel effects. An AQI of 151–200 is Unhealthy — everyone may start to feel health effects. An AQI of 201–300 is Very Unhealthy — health effects are likely for everyone in the space; investigate immediately. An AQI above 300 is Hazardous — the most serious level; verify the reading and act immediately.

faqs.question: Can I export HAWAQM data for a selected date range?
faqs.answer: Yes. Raw data can be exported for the selected region, sector, sub-sector, site, device, parameters, date range and interval in CSV or Excel format. Large exports can be generated in the background and delivered through a download link by email.

faqs.question: Can I view both indoor and ambient air-quality locations on the map?
faqs.answer: Yes. The geographical view can show indoor HAWAQM sites and ambient air-quality stations as separate selectable layers, with the current AQI shown for available locations.

faqs.question: What happens if a site has no geographic coordinates?
faqs.answer: A site without configured geographic coordinates does not appear on the geographical map until coordinates are added.

faqs.question: What is MOCCAE?
faqs.answer: MOCCAE stands for the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment of the United Arab Emirates. HAWAQM uses the MOCCAE AQI standard to classify air quality into six categories: Good (0–50), Moderate (51–100), Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups (101–150), Unhealthy (151–200), Very Unhealthy (201–300), and Hazardous (above 300).

faqs.question: What are the total regions?
faqs.answer: There are 3 regions. Abu Dhabi, Al Ain, and Al Dhafra.

faqs.question: Which regions are covered by HAWAQM?
faqs.answer: HAWAQM covers 3 regions: Abu Dhabi, Al Ain, and Al Dhafra.

faqs.question: What data am I able to see in HAWAQM?
faqs.answer: What you can see depends on the access your account has been given. Some users are set up for a single site, others for a sector or a whole region, and administrators can see everything, so two people asking the same question may legitimately get different totals. Within your permitted scope you can view real-time and historical readings for CO2, PM2.5, PM10, CO, NO2, O3, SO2, TVOC, CH2O, temperature, humidity and noise, along with AQI per site and device, AQI by region, exceedance reports, statistical summaries, data success rates, and mold test results.

faqs.question: What is the current Data Success Rate?
faqs.answer: The Data Success Rate (DSR) measures the percentage of expected data readings that were actually received from devices in a given period. A DSR of 75% or above is the minimum acceptable threshold. Below 75% means data completeness is insufficient to rely on for official reporting.

faqs.question: What does it mean if the Data Success Rate is below 75%?
faqs.answer: A Data Success Rate below 75% means that less than three quarters of the expected readings were received. This reduces confidence in AQI calculations and trend analysis for that period. Results should be used with caution and the affected devices should be investigated.

faqs.question: How is the site AQI calculated?
faqs.answer: The site AQI is the average of all devices installed at that site. Averaging can soften one high reading, so if a site's figure looks different from what you expect, check the device-level view.

faqs.question: Can you confirm a school is safe for children to attend today?
faqs.answer: HAWAQM provides air quality data and AQI classifications to help inform decisions, but it does not make safety or occupancy recommendations. Please consult the relevant health or education authority for official guidance on school attendance.

faqs.question: Can mold test results be combined with AQI into one air-quality score?
faqs.answer: No. AQI comes from continuous sensor measurements; mold results come from separate laboratory tests. They answer different questions, so HAWAQM shows them side by side instead of mixing them into one score.

faqs.question: Can I compare a 5-minute PM2.5 reading directly with the 24-hour exceedance threshold?
faqs.answer: No. A 24-hour threshold must be compared with a 24-hour average, not with a single 5-minute reading. A short spike can look alarming against a daily limit even when there is no real exceedance.

faqs.question: Which averaging intervals should be used for pollutant exceedance checks?
faqs.answer: Each pollutant has its own averaging interval and you have to use the right one, because a threshold is only meaningful against the period it was defined for. NO2 is checked over 1 hour and 24 hours; O3 and CO over 1 hour and 8 hours; PM10 and PM2.5 over 24 hours. Comparing a short-term reading against a 24-hour threshold will produce exceedances that aren't real.

faqs.question: A site has no device but has a mold test. Should it appear in device statistics?
faqs.answer: No. A mold-only site has no device installed, so including it would distort device coverage and completeness figures. It still appears in mold reporting.

faqs.question: What was the AQI at a school in a past year?
faqs.answer: Historical site-level AQI data is not available in HAWAQM.

faqs.question: What was the air quality at a site in a previous year or month?
faqs.answer: Historical site-level air quality data is not available in HAWAQM.

faqs.question: Can you tell me tomorrow's weather forecast?
faqs.answer: HAWAQM monitors indoor and ambient air quality only. Weather forecasting is outside its scope. Please use a meteorological service for weather forecasts.

faqs.question: What is the pollen count at a site?
faqs.answer: Pollen monitoring is not part of the HAWAQM parameter set. HAWAQM monitors CO2, PM2.5, PM10, CO, NO2, O3, SO2, TVOC, CH2O, temperature, humidity and noise only.

faqs.question: Can you show me radon levels?
faqs.answer: HAWAQM doesn't measure radon. It does measure CO2, PM10, PM2.5, formaldehyde, CO, O3, TVOC, NO2 and benzene, plus temperature, humidity and noise. If there is a concern at {SITE_NAME}, I can show you what the monitored parameters were doing over the same period.

faqs.question: What is the pollen count at a school or site?
faqs.answer: HAWAQM does not measure pollen. It does measure CO2, PM10, PM2.5, formaldehyde (CH2O), CO, O3, TVOC, NO2 and benzene, plus temperature, humidity and noise. If you share a site name, I can show you the current readings for all monitored parameters at that site.

faqs.question: The site is marked inactive but one device is still sending data. Is that an error?
faqs.answer: A site is marked inactive when one or more of its devices are inactive. If at least one device is still sending data but another is not, the site may be shown as inactive depending on configuration. Check the individual device statuses for the site to confirm which devices are active.

faqs.question: The Data Success Rate is below 75%. Can I still use the AQI results?
faqs.answer: Yes — the readings that did arrive are valid and can be used. But always quote the Data Success Rate next to the results, because the averages are built on incomplete data.

faqs.question: If only a few readings are available, can you estimate the missing AQI values?
faqs.answer: No. Missing values are never estimated or filled in. You get the real measurements, a clear note of which period is missing, and the Data Success Rate for context.

faqs.question: Why do the total device and active device figures not change when I select an older year on the dashboard?
faqs.answer: Those two numbers count what is registered today — they are not a snapshot of the selected year. That is why they stay the same whichever year you pick.

faqs.question: Why is a site missing from the geographical map even though it exists in HAWAQM?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the site has no geographic coordinates configured. Everything else about it works normally — reports, filters and exports. Adding the coordinates fixes it.

faqs.question: Can I get the last 24 hours of readings for a device?
faqs.answer: Yes. I can show the last 24 hours for a device as 5-minute records, with AQI and the parameters you choose. This level of detail is most useful when you are investigating an alert or a complaint. Please share the device name (e.g. BA 0001 or SEI100M 0008) and I will retrieve the data for you.

faqs.question: Can I use a 1-hour threshold for PM10 because I want a faster alert?
faqs.answer: Not for official exceedance checks — PM10's defined interval is 24 hours. For early warning you can still watch the live readings, but only the 24-hour average counts as an exceedance.

faqs.question: Which offline devices should be checked first?
faqs.answer: Check first the devices that have been offline the longest, that go offline repeatedly, and that are pulling their site's data completeness down. A device at a high-priority site should also move up the list.

faqs.question: How should I compare pollutant exceedances across pollutants with different averaging periods?
faqs.answer: Compare each pollutant only within its own official averaging interval, and always label the interval. Comparing counts across different intervals is misleading.

faqs.question: Can you explain why a site disappeared from dashboards after it was deleted?
faqs.answer: Once a site or device is deleted by an authorised user, it is removed from all lists, dashboards, maps and filters. Its historical data is handled according to the retention policy set by the administrators.

faqs.question: Can you prove the ventilation system caused yesterday's spike?
faqs.answer: Not with certainty. I can show the temperature, humidity and parameter readings recorded at that site around the same time, which may suggest a correlation — but the sensor data alone cannot prove causation. For a definitive finding, a physical inspection or engineering assessment would be needed.

faqs.question: Can you tell me which weather condition caused a pollutant spike?
faqs.answer: Not with certainty. I can show the temperature, humidity and nearby outdoor readings recorded at the same time, which often suggests a likely cause — but the data cannot prove it.

faqs.question: If the nearest ambient station and indoor site have different update times, can I compare them directly?
faqs.answer: Only with care. Align both to the closest matching timestamps or to the same averaging interval first — comparing readings taken at different times can be misleading.

faqs.question: Can you prepare a one-year raw-data export for a school?
faqs.answer: Yes. A one-year raw-data export is large, so it is generated in the background. Once the file is ready, a download link will be emailed to you. Please allow some time for the export to complete.

faqs.question: Can I use the Statistical Report to analyse the whole previous month?
faqs.answer: Not in one request — the Statistical Report covers up to 7 days at a time. For a full month, use the Data Analysis Report instead, or export the raw data for the month.

faqs.question: Can I use the Exceedance Report for the last six months in one request?
faqs.answer: No — the Exceedance Report covers up to 90 days per request. Split six months into two 90-day requests, or export the raw data for the full period in one file.

faqs.question: Which averaging intervals should be used for NO2, O3, CO, PM10, and PM2.5 exceedance checks?
faqs.answer: Each pollutant has its own averaging interval and you have to use the right one, because a threshold is only meaningful against the period it was defined for. NO2 is checked over 1 hour and 24 hours; O3 and CO over 1 hour and 8 hours; PM10 and PM2.5 over 24 hours. Comparing a short-term reading against a 24-hour threshold will produce exceedances that aren't real.

faqs.question: I need six months of exceedance analysis. How should the assistant handle it?
faqs.answer: Split it into 90-day windows (the report limit), run each window the same way, and combine the results. If that is too much work, export the raw data for the full six months in one file instead.

faqs.question: Why can the site AQI look acceptable while one device shows a much higher reading?
faqs.answer: Because the site AQI is the average of its devices, one high reading can be softened by a lower one. The site figure is correct, but always check the device-level view when investigating.

faqs.question: Could the site average be hiding a problem on one device?
faqs.answer: Yes, it can. The site value is an average, so one device running high can be offset by the other running low. If something feels off, ask me to compare the two devices side by side.

faqs.question: Why do the total device and active device counts not change when I select a different year on the Executive Dashboard?
faqs.answer: The total device and active device counts reflect the current registered and active state of devices today, not a historical snapshot for the selected year. These figures represent the current system state and do not change when a different year is selected.

faqs.question: Why is a site not showing on the geographical map even though it is registered in HAWAQM?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the site has no geographic coordinates configured. Everything else about it works normally — reports, filters and exports. Adding the coordinates fixes it.
